newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 3.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.
- Government parties will not take a decision on an abortion referendum before the general election.
- Advances by rebels in eastern Zaire raise fears of a fresh refugee crisis after up to 170,000 refugees flee their camps to avoid fierce fighting.
- Weekend of rioting in Albania leaves 14 dead.
- Up to 1,000 new jobs are expected in the est of Ireland as part of 38 million Irish pound expansion by Boston Scientific Corporation in Galway over next three years.
- The contract between Radio Ireland and the Independent Radio and Television Commission will be signed only after new chief is named, following the recent ousting of former chief.
- Taxpayers face 200 million Irish pound compensation bill for soldiers alleging damaged hearing.
- The Government is expected to increase its proposed 20,000 Irish pound cap on credit union loans in a new bill before parliament ollowing pressure from the Irish League of Credit Unions.
- Swimmer Michelle Smith's first race in Ireland since her triple Olympic gold in Atlanta was soured when the question of drug-taking dominated a post-race press conference.
- Financial markets expected to comb key labour data in the U.S. and Germany in the coming weeks for clues to the timing of the next U.S. rate rise and European economic and monetary union (EMU).
